transcript.text: Hello Mr Evans, my name is Dr Rossi, I'm one of the junior doctors. Is it OK if I ask you some questions? What's brought you in today?
It's in the middle of my chest, feels like an elephant sitting on me, and hasn't gone away even though I've been resting. I'm really worried because my dad died of a heart attack at 60.
Does the pain go anywhere?
Yeah, it goes into my left arm and up into my jaw, too.
I can see this is really frightening. When exactly did it start, what does it feel like, and how bad is it out of ten?
It's an eight out of ten. Worst pain I've ever had.
Have you had any sweating, feeling sick or shortness of breath with it?
I've been sweating buckets and I feel a bit sick. Bit short of breath too.
Is it worse when you breathe in or move, is it a tearing pain going through to your back, and have you had any recent long trips or leg swelling?
It doesn't hurt more when I breathe in or move around, and it's not tearing. No long flights recently, and my legs aren't swollen.
Have you had any pain like this before, for example when walking?
Yeah, for a few weeks I'd get this tightness when walking up hills, but it would go away after I rested for a couple of minutes. I thought it was just getting old.
Do you smoke, and have you ever been told you have high blood pressure, high cholesterol or diabetes?
I smoke about 20 a day. I was told my blood pressure was high a while back but never went back for tablets. Not diabetic as far as I know.
Does anyone in your family have heart problems?
My dad died of a heart attack when he was 60.
Do you take any medications, and do you have any allergies?
I don't take anything regularly. No allergies.

transcript.finding: HR 96 regular, BP 158/94 in both arms, RR 20, SpO2 96% on air, temperature 36.8°C.

transcript.result: 2 mm ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL.

transcript.text: I know you're worried because of what happened to your dad, and I'm taking this very seriously. The heart tracing shows your heart is under strain, so I'm getting my senior doctor now, we'll give you something for the pain and some aspirin, and the heart team will likely need to open up an artery. Is that OK?
Oh, thank you, doctor. That must be really serious, but I'm glad you're taking it seriously. Can you tell me if the pain will go away soon after the pills? I'm so worried it's my heart.

postAnswers.question: What is the most likely diagnosis?
postAnswers.answer: An acute inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (inferior STEMI).

postAnswers.question: What is your immediate management?
postAnswers.answer: Call for senior help and activate the primary PCI pathway. Give aspirin 300 mg, analgesia such as IV morphine with an antiemetic, oxygen only if hypoxic, GTN if not hypotensive, IV access, bloods and continuous monitoring.
